pr_body:
- Added the `mv_percentile(values, percentile)` function
- Used as a surrogate in the `percentile(column, percentile)` aggregation
- Updated docs to specify that the surrogate _should_ be implemented if possible

The same way as mv_median does, this yields exact results (Ignoring double operations error).
For that, some decisions were made, specially in the long evaluator (Check the comments in context in `MvPercentile.java`)

Closes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/111591

Wow, good catch.
Some tests are failing in the CI because of weird things like pages having blocks with different position counts, so I think you found the culprit... 

And I thought I was testing sorted values in unit tests, but there may be something wrong there. Gonna check
Added an assertion to AbstractScalarTestCase for the block positions, and it now failed successfully!
Percentile seems to require a foldable `percentile` value. Just curious why mv_percentile can accept even fields.

In the agg case, it's because it's "impossible" for it to not be foldable (Unless it appears in the grouping, which is a case I'm not sure we're allowing btw).
The evaluator however, can handle them without problem, so I think it's better to just allow it. Simpler function, less arbitrary restrictions

I'm not saying it's wrong, but maybe suggest to look at this from a different angle: language consistency. If one function does it one way and the other does it differently, we should try to be consistent and have the same behavior; this makes it less confusing for users and easier to use/adopt.

The consistent way for me would be to not force foldables on non-agg functions, as they all can be evaluated whether foldable or not. If I as a user tried to use a field in a function, and it told me that it must be a constant, _that_ would be confusing 👀 
For aggs, it's a logical problem, as they need X fields to accumulate, and Y fields as configuration.

So I'm really not seeing the problem of having non-foldable fields. I feel like we would be placing arbitrary restrictions

Since `PERCENTILE` has to hit the whole index it has to be foldable. `MV_PERCENTILE` doesn't really have to be. But it's certainly kindest if, when it is, we can fail the query up front for invalid stuff.

I'm kind of ambivalent on forcing it to be foldable - I like that if we force it now we can always un-force it later. We can't go the other way. But in a lot of ways that's actually more work for a less flexible system.
I wonder if those are too much... As it's adding 4 times the amount of cases

Interesting! I can see why you'd do it. What's the runtime difference on one of the tests? I can imagine it's a few seconds so it's worth it.

As to avoid duplicating the exact logic there's in the original function, I'm always using BigDecimals gere to generate the cases (Except for ints, which is trivial).

+    private static Number calculatePercentile(List<Number> rawValues, double percentile) {
+        if (rawValues.isEmpty() || percentile < 0 || percentile > 100) {
+            return null;
+        }
+
+        if (rawValues.size() == 1) {
+            return rawValues.get(0);
+        }
+
+        int valueCount = rawValues.size();
+        var p = percentile / 100.0;
+        var index = p * (valueCount - 1);
+        var lowerIndex = (int) index;
+        var upperIndex = lowerIndex + 1;
+        var fraction = index - lowerIndex;
+
+        if (rawValues.get(0) instanceof Integer) {
+            var values = rawValues.stream().mapToInt(Number::intValue).sorted().toArray();
+
+            if (percentile == 0) {
+                return values[0];
+            } else if (percentile == 100) {
+                return values[valueCount - 1];
+            } else {
+                assert lowerIndex >= 0 && upperIndex < valueCount;
+                var difference = (long) values[upperIndex] - values[lowerIndex];
+                return values[lowerIndex] + (int) (fraction * difference);
+            }
+        }
+
+        if (rawValues.get(0) instanceof Long) {
+            var values = rawValues.stream().mapToLong(Number::longValue).sorted().toArray();
+
+            if (percentile == 0) {
+                return values[0];
+            } else if (percentile == 100) {
+                return values[valueCount - 1];
+            } else {
+                assert lowerIndex >= 0 && upperIndex < valueCount;
+                return calculatePercentile(fraction, new BigDecimal(values[lowerIndex]), new BigDecimal(values[upperIndex])).longValue();
+            }
+        }
+
+        if (rawValues.get(0) instanceof Double) {
+            var values = rawValues.stream().mapToDouble(Number::doubleValue).sorted().toArray();
+
+            if (percentile == 0) {
+                return values[0];
+            } else if (percentile == 100) {
+                return values[valueCount - 1];
+            } else {
+                assert lowerIndex >= 0 && upperIndex < valueCount;
+                return calculatePercentile(fraction, new BigDecimal(values[lowerIndex]), new BigDecimal(values[upperIndex])).doubleValue();
+            }
+        }
+
+        throw new IllegalArgumentException("Unsupported type: " + rawValues.get(0).getClass());
